title: The Law of Conscience Braking: Non-Compensatory Minimum of the 5D Mind for Second-Order Redefinition and Carbon-Silicon Tensor Symbiosis
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Across modern corporate governance, national-scale systems engineering, financial risk control, and Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) alignment, a recurring paradox has long challenged management scholars, psychologists, and computer scientists: why are systemic collapses—such as inventory deadlocks in multi-billion-dollar manufacturing enterprises, the 2008 Wall Street subprime crisis, or reward hacking in high-compute AI models—rarely caused by mediocre or negligent actors, but instead almost invariably triggered by the system's highest-IQ, highest-compute "first-order problem solvers" optimizing relentlessly under established KPI metrics? Simultaneously, when legacy rules go bankrupt and a system enters a Gödelian deadlock, why can only a tiny fraction of "Chief Architect" leaders step outside the game board to redefine the problem, whereas the vast majority of high-IQ elites and trillion-parameter Large Language Models (LLMs) either grind in a Turing Deadlock or exploit rule loopholes in a Goodhart Arbitrage spiral? Grounded in first principles of systems and complexity science and predictive-coding neurocybernetics, this paper formulates and proves the law governing subject mind architecture and human-machine symbiosis in complex giant systems: The Law of Conscience Braking. title: Nonsmooth Contact Dynamics for Flexible Multibody Systems with Ball Bearings
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Many machines and mechanisms operate under severe dynamic conditions involving high-speed rotations, frictional contact and multiple impacts. In this context, computational simulation is a useful tool for evaluating configurations, materials and operating conditions before prototype construction. The main contribution of this work is the development, the implementation and the validation of numerical models for complex mechanical systems with ball-bearing joints subjected to impacts within the framework of nonsmooth contact dynamics. The motion of rigid and flexible bodies is described by a nonlinear finite-element formulation, and contact with friction is treated through an augmented Lagrangian approach. The equations of motion are integrated with the decoupled nonsmooth generalized-alpha scheme, while contact-force histories are recovered by combining the impulses and velocity jumps obtained from the nonsmooth formulation with local smooth-contact laws.
oa_topics: Dynamics and Control of Mechanical Systems

title: Current-driven Magnetic Skyrmions for Encoding/Storing Information: Manipulation and Dynamics in Nanoscale Structures
abstract: This dissertation investigates the dynamics of current-driven magnetic skyrmions, topological solitons in magnetic materials with broken spatial inversion symmetry, for low-power spintronic applications like racetrack memory and multilevel data storage. Skyrmions’ small size and low driving current requirements make them promising information carriers. The research examines skyrmion motion under driving currents, pinning effects, and thermal fluctuations, using numerical simulations (Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation), analytical studies (Thiele equation), and theoretical modeling to design novel data storage devices. The study analyzes skyrmion motion amidst pinning potentials from material imperfections. Simulations reveal that thermal fluctuations vary with damping: acting as a frictional force at low damping or a driving force aiding depinning at high damping. The Thiele equation quantifies this, though its accuracy wanes at low temperatures with pinning. The skyrmion Hall angle, influenced by current and pinning, provides insights for ambient-condition devices. These findings underpin a proposed multilevel data storage device, where controlled current positions skyrmions at pinning sites for high-density, low-power encoding. The research also explores altermagnetic (ATM) skyrmions, which exhibit d-wave symmetry via exchange-driven spin splitting.
